summary.en: Generate subsets by index, prune nonnegative sums safely, and compare recursion with bitmask enumeration.
summary.bn: ইনডেক্স ধরে সাবসেট বানাও, অঋণাত্মক সংখ্যায় বাড়তি যোগফলের পথ বাদ দাও, আর bitmask দিয়েও গুনে দেখো।

notes: The demonstrated programs use C17; the lesson states their input and arithmetic bounds.

sections.title: Every item gets a yes-or-no choice
Track an index and a partial sum
Pruning depends on the input domain
Read the mask as an index set
One path for each indexed subset
Listing and deciding have different costs
Zeros and repeated values are real choices
Do not borrow an invalid prune

examples.title: Print all nonnegative target subsets
examples.explanationHtml: The first program prints indices 2 and then indices 0 1 for target five. Its count is two. The empty indexed set is printed as Indices: with nothing after the colon.

examples.title: Enumerate masks with signed values
examples.explanationHtml: The second program accepts negative values and tries every mask. For [-2,0,2] at target zero, it counts four subsets. It applies no overshoot prune, so cancellation remains possible.

examples.title: Merge equal reachability states
examples.explanationHtml: The last program marks reachable totals for [2,3,5]. Downward totals prevent one item from being reused in the same iteration. This Boolean table lists totals, not the subsets that achieve them.

practice.title: Print indexed subsets reaching a target
practice.statementHtml:
Input: n, target, then nonnegative values (n 0..16, values/target 0..100):

Output: Print the prompt, each Indices: line in exclude-first order, then Count:.
hints: Keep the state convention and stopping rule described in Subset Sum and Subsets.
Include and exclude decisions enumerate subsets by index.

practice.title: Count signed subsets by masks
practice.statementHtml:
Input: n, target, then values (n 0..16, values/target -100..100):

Output: Print the prompt, then Count: for indexed subsets, including the empty subset.
hints: Keep the state convention and stopping rule described in Subset Sum and Subsets.
The empty subset has sum zero.

practice.title: Why must sum==target not end counting immediately for values [0,0] and target zero?
practice.statementHtml: Why must sum==target not end counting immediately for values [0,0] and target zero?
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: The empty subset, each singleton index and both indices are four different subsets. Reaching zero before the last decision leaves unresolved zero choices. Test equality at complete leaves to count all four.

practice.title: Show a counterexample to pruning sum>target when negative numbers are allowed.
practice.statementHtml: Show a counterexample to pruning sum>target when negative numbers are allowed.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: For values [7,-2] and target 5, including 7 temporarily exceeds the target. Including -2 completes a valid subset. The overshoot prune would discard that answer.

quiz.prompt: How many indexed subsets does a three-item array have?
quiz.explanation: Every index has two choices, giving 2 cubed subsets including the empty one.

quiz.prompt: Which subset corresponds to mask zero?
quiz.explanation: No bit is set, so no index is selected.

quiz.prompt: When is sum greater than target a safe pruning reason?
options: When every remaining value is nonnegative
quiz.explanation: A nonnegative continuation cannot decrease the current sum.

quiz.prompt: How many indexed subsets of [0,0] sum to zero?
quiz.explanation: The two zero-valued indices remain distinct: empty, first, second, both.

quiz.prompt: For values [2,3,5], which index subset is visited first by exclude-before-include at target five?
quiz.explanation: Excluding indices zero and one reaches the singleton at index two first.

quiz.prompt: Why use an unsigned mask and restrict n below its bit width?
quiz.explanation: A shift count at least the type width is undefined; small n avoids that hazard.

quiz.prompt: What distinguishes subset-sum DP from the recursive enumeration here?
quiz.explanation: A reachability table reuses state answers instead of revisiting every decision path.

quiz.prompt: Which indexed sum is selected by mask five for values [2,3,5]?
quiz.explanation: Binary 101 selects indices zero and two: two plus five.

quiz.prompt: How many masks are checked for an empty subset instance?
quiz.explanation: Even with no items, mask zero represents one empty subset.

quiz.prompt: What sum remains after including and then removing value three?
quiz.explanation: The undo returns to the original partial sum of two.

keyPoints.en: Include and exclude decisions enumerate subsets by index.
keyPoints.bn: নেবে কি নেবে না, এই দুই সিদ্ধান্তে ইনডেক্স ধরে সাবসেট পাও।

keyPoints.en: The empty subset has sum zero.
Nonnegative values make the sum-exceeds-target prune safe.
keyPoints.bn: সব মান অঋণাত্মক হলে টার্গেটের বেশি যোগফলের পথ বাদ দেওয়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Negative values can repair a large partial sum.
keyPoints.bn: ঋণাত্মক মান পরে যোগ হলে বড় আংশিক যোগফলও কমতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: A bitmask uses one bit per item and includes mask zero.
keyPoints.bn: bitmask-এ প্রতি আইটেমের জন্য একটা বিট থাকে, আর শূন্য মাস্কও ধরতে হয়।

examQuestions.answerHtml: The empty subset, each singleton index and both indices are four different subsets. Reaching zero before the last decision leaves unresolved zero choices. Test equality at complete leaves to count all four.

examQuestions.question: State the invariant and justify the time and space costs of Subset Sum and Subsets.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
The recursion invariant states that sum equals the selected values before pos. Excluding an item leaves it unchanged. Including the item adds exactly values[pos]. Both branches advance pos, so they cannot select the same index twice.

Each indexed subset defines a unique sequence of include-or-exclude choices. The full recursion follows that sequence. On nonnegative input, a subset reaching the target never has a prefix sum above the target, so the prune cannot discard its route. At a complete leaf, equality decides precisely whether it is reported.

A mask gives the same uniqueness argument through its bits. Distinct masks differ at an index and therefore represent distinct indexed subsets. Equal values do not merge those indices. If you instead want distinct value multisets, you need an additional duplicate-handling rule and a different counting specification.

There are 2^n masks and each scans n positions, giving O(n*2^n) time. The recursion visits O(2^n) nodes before pruning, but printing a subset may take O(n), so the same upper bound covers all output. Recursion and its chosen array need O(n) extra space.

For nonnegative integer target T, a Boolean DP can decide reachability in O(nT) time and O(T) memory. That may beat enumeration when T is moderate. It may be worse when numeric values are huge and n is small.

The O(nT) bound is pseudo-polynomial: binary encoding stores T in about log2(T) bits. A table of size T can be exponential in that length. This distinction will matter when you study NP-completeness. It does not make the practical table useless.
